headline: Six weeks of scans cleared — 120 new models, and a leaderboard that now needs a comparability rule

insights.title: Nine scan PRs, ~193 papers read, 120 accepted
insights.body: The 08-19 through 09-16 scans were processed one PR at a time, every candidate read from its PDF under a shared rule set. The tracker grew from 414 to 534 models. Rejections held to the same line as before: benchmarks, surveys, analysis papers, and wrappers over frozen policies — many quoted their own 'no parameters are updated' in the abstract. Titles kept misleading both ways: EffVLA, FlashVLA and ActSafeGuard read like analysis or runtime papers but train real weights.

insights.title: LIBERO top-13 reshuffles: V-Link #4, ProWAM #8, StructRL #11
insights.body: V-Link (GR00T N1.6 + query tokens restoring DiT visual features) enters at 99.33, ProWAM (Wan2.2-5B world-action model) at 99.05 and StructRL at 98.95; MPCoT and LIRA drop out. ProWAM is also RoboTwin v2 #4 at 93.4 on the standard multi-task protocol. INDI takes SimplerEnv #2 (84.7) and GIFT-Feature takes RoboCasa #1 (82.3).

insights.title: Two ranking pitfalls caught mid-run
insights.body: LM-X's RoboTwin score was the hard split only, yet the builder's fallback averaged it into robotwin_v2_avg against Easy+Hard means — moved out and a rule added. Scan PRs kept re-proposing already-accepted papers and overwriting their real YAMLs with draft stubs; the stub cleanup was changed to delete only new files and restore overwrites, and every merge was checked against main.

insights.title: Open question: what counts as the same benchmark
insights.body: RoboCasa ranks Kitchen-24 and GR1-Tabletop-24 results together (GIFT-Feature #1 is GR1; Z-1 #2 is Kitchen). RoboTwin v2 ranks some paper-reported task-subset averages while excluding single-split and small-subset runs. Both need a single rule before the rankings in those two benchmarks can be read as like-for-like.
